description.narrative:
Activity aims to strengthen institutional capacities for fighting illicit trafficking of cultural property and reinforce partnerships in targeted countries of the English and Dutch speaking Caribbean through capacity-building, technical advice and participatory processes, as well as advocacy in ratification of the 1970 and UNIDROIT Conventions by countries in the Caribbean SIDS.
1970 Convention had been ratified by few Caribbean nations of The Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Grenada and Haiti. Jamaica is not yet a signatory though it is moving towards ratification conducting national workshop in 2018. No Caribbean country has yet signed the 1995 UNIDROIT Convention. The importance of ratifying the 1970 and UNIDROIT Conventions by countries in the Caribbean will be addressed through awareness raising.
The activity will allow national actors from relevant Ministries, museums, police and customs, archives and libraries, art professionals, art dealers, law enforcement officials, etc. of the Caribbean to discuss policies and practices needed to combat illicit trafficking in cultural property at the national and sub-regional levels. It will allow countries to implement, as part of their national cultural heritage protection policy, its national restitution program, national capacity-building action with technical support from UNESCO to create a common platform for sub-regional collaboration to combat illicit trafficking of cultural properties.
